articles.title: Frances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield’s relationship: From young tennis players to a decade of love and support
articles.summary: International Sports News: Frances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield’s relationship has grown alongside his tennis career. What started with a meeting through a mutual friend in 2015 h.
articles.body: Frances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield’s relationship has grown alongside his tennis career. What started with a meeting through a mutual friend in 2015 has turned into a decade-long partnership filled with big wins, difficult moments, travel and plenty of memories.Broomfield has been there through some of the biggest moments of Tiafoe’s career, often watching from the player’s box and sharing the emotions that come with life on the ATP Tour.2015: Frances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield’s relationship beginsFrances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield met through a mutual friend in 2015, when they were both young tennis players. Tiafoe was starting to make his mark in professional tennis, while Broomfield was building her own path in the sport.Their relationship became public later that year. In December, Tiafoe shared a sweet Instagram post about Broomfield and wrote about missing her during the holidays.At the time, neither knew just how much their lives would change in the years ahead.2017–2019: Frances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield grow closer togetherIn 2017, Tiafoe celebrated their second anniversary with a loving tribute to Broomfield. A year later, they spent Valentine’s Day together in France, with Broomfield describing Tiafoe as her partner and best friend.Their careers were also moving forward. In 2019, Tiafoe traveled to Los Angeles for Broomfield’s UCLA Senior Day. That same year, she and Gabby Andrews won the NCAA women’s doubles championship.Tiafoe proudly celebrated her achievement, showing that their support has always gone both ways.2020–2021: Frances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield’s life beyond tennisTheir relationship continued to grow away from the court too. In 2020, they celebrated Broomfield’s 21st birthday.Then came King Richard. Broomfield worked as a tennis body double for Venus Williams in the movie’s tennis scenes, putting her own tennis experience to work on the project. Tiafoe joined her at the film’s Los Angeles premiere in November 2021.It was another moment where their personal and professional worlds came together.2022: Ayan Broomfield supports Frances Tiafoe through his US Open breakthroughThe 2022 US Open changed Frances Tiafoe’s career forever.He defeated Rafael Nadal and Andrey Rublev before reaching the semifinals, where he pushed Carlos Alcaraz to a thrilling five-set match. Broomfield was there as he experienced the biggest run of his career at that point.Speaking to the ATP Tour, she later called those two weeks “magical” and said the experience changed their lives and the lives of Tiafoe’s family.She also explained why they work so well together. Tiafoe is naturally happy-go-lucky, while she is more serious and grounded. That difference, she said, helps them balance each other.2023–2024: Frances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield celebrate career milestones togetherWhen Tiafoe broke into the ATP top 10 in 2023, Ayan Broomfield celebrated the achievement online. She revealed that she had saved screenshots of his milestones, waiting for the day he would reach that level.Tiafoe responded by thanking her for staying beside him through “the good, the bad and the standstills.”In 2024, she continued supporting him at major tournaments, including Wimbledon and the US Open. During the US Open, she sat beside Tiafoe’s mother in the player’s box, holding hands and sharing the tension of his matches.Away from tennis, the couple continued making memories, including a 2024 Kansas City Chiefs game where they met Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce.2025–2026: Frances Tiafoe and Ayan Broomfield remain by each other’s sideAfter nearly a decade together, Broomfield remains one of the most familiar faces in Tiafoe’s corner.She continues to attend tournaments, cheer for him and use humor to make the pressure of tennis a little lighter. Tiafoe, meanwhile, has repeatedly celebrated her as his “rock” and someone he is deeply thankful to have in his life.As another US Open approaches, their story feels especially meaningful. Broomfield has seen Tiafoe before the fame, before the biggest wins and before the pressure that comes with being one of America’s top tennis stars.She has been there through all of it. And perhaps that is what makes their relationship so special, not simply that they have celebrated the highs together, but that they have continued choosing each other through every stage of the journey.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How did Elena Rybakina build her $20 million fortune? The incredible rise that made her one of tennis' biggest earners
articles.summary: International Sports News: Elena Rybakina has turned a quiet personality and powerful tennis game into a fortune estimated at $20 million. Her wealth did not arrive overnight. I.
articles.body: Elena Rybakina has turned a quiet personality and powerful tennis game into a fortune estimated at $20 million. Her wealth did not arrive overnight. It grew through years of grinding on the professional circuit, major Grand Slam success and a growing list of commercial partnerships. From a young player facing financial limits to one of tennis' biggest stars, Rybakina's rise has been both remarkable and highly rewarding.Elena Rybakina's $20 million fortune grew with Grand Slam successRybakina's biggest financial breakthrough came with her 2022 Wimbledon triumph. At just 23, she defeated Ons Jabeur in the final to become the first player representing Kazakhstan to win a Grand Slam singles title. The victory changed her status in tennis and gave her career a powerful commercial lift.But Wimbledon was only the beginning. Rybakina followed it with a run to the 2023 Australian Open final and then captured WTA 1000 titles at Indian Wells and Rome. Her ability to compete across hard courts, clay and grass helped turn her into a regular contender at the biggest tournaments.Her prize money accelerated sharply as her results improved. According to Celebrity Net Worth, Rybakina has collected more than $30 million in official tournament prize money during her career, which is already greater than the site's estimated $20 million net worth. That difference highlights an important point: career earnings and net worth are not the same thing.The 2025 WTA Finals delivered one of her most remarkable paydays. Rybakina went unbeaten through the tournament and defeated world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in the final. Her perfect 5-0 campaign earned her $5.235 million, described by the source as a record prize for a women's professional sporting event at the time.Her momentum continued into 2026. Rybakina won her second Grand Slam at the Australian Open, defeating Sabalenka in a dramatic three-set final. She later won Stuttgart again and reached her first US Open final. That run also secured her rise to world No. 1 for the first time.Elena Rybakina's endorsements add another major income streamTournament winnings are only one part of Rybakina's financial success. Her profile has also attracted major brands, particularly after her Wimbledon breakthrough.Her endorsement portfolio has included Yonex, Red Bull, Lexus, Bank RBK, KAZ Minerals, Fanatics, Topps and Swiss watchmaker Vanguart. Yonex has been especially visible, providing her racquets, clothing and footwear.Rybakina's appeal is interesting because she has never relied heavily on a loud public persona. Her calm approach on court has become part of her identity. Instead, her biggest selling point is performance. Grand Slam titles, deep tournament runs and a world No. 1 ranking have steadily increased her value to sponsors.Her journey also adds another layer to the story. Born in Moscow, Rybakina switched to representing Kazakhstan in 2018 after the country's tennis federation offered financial and developmental support. That backing helped give her the stability needed to pursue elite tennis.Today, the combination of prize money, sponsorships and years of success has helped establish Rybakina as one of the highest-earning names in women's tennis. Her estimated $20 million fortune reflects not just one breakthrough, but the financial rewards of building a sustained career at the very top of the sport.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open 2026 results: How Alexander Zverev turned tears into triumph in New York
articles.summary: How a more composed Alexander Zverev stayed 'zen-like' to beat Ben Shelton and win the US Open, six years after a heart-breaking defeat in the final.
articles.body:
As he stepped up to the baseline, Alexander Zverev could be forgiven for letting his mind slip back to the last time he served for the US Open title.

Six years ago, the German top seed threw away a two-set lead in a devastating loss to Dominic Thiem, having served for the match in the fifth set.

This time, instead of his own nerves, it was American Ben Shelton and the majority of the 24,000-strong crowd that stood in Zverev's way.

But this was a different Zverev: a Grand Slam champion now, having won the French Open in June.

Such was his focus that he did not initially realise he had sealed a 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 victory.

After firing down another unstoppable serve to win the match, Zverev returned to the baseline ready to start the next point - only to be told by his team the match was over.

"In that moment I was in the zone a lot. I didn't hear noise at all," Zverev said.

"It's funny - tennis teachers always tell you to just play the next point and forget about the score.

"At that moment I forgot about the score and it helped me."

As the realisation sunk in, the 29-year-old broke into a broad and slightly surprised smile before raising his arms above his head.

It was a direct contrast to his defeat by Thiem in 2020, where a tearful Zverev said during the trophy presentation: "I wish one day I can bring the trophy home."

"We went 30 years without winning a Grand Slam title and now we've won two in three months," said Zverev.

"2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before."

Zverev's parents were not there for his previous final at Flushing Meadows, but his father and coach Alexander senior was on the sidelines this time.

As well as paying tribute to his father, Zverev also thanked his mother for her support following his type 1 diabetes diagnosis as a child.

"When doctors tell you that life and sports will be very limited for that child, it takes a very strong mother to say 'my son will be whatever he wants to be'," Zverev said.

"My mother is the most important and strongest person I know."

Zverev caps transformational year with US Open triumph

All About US Open: Zverev claims second Grand Slam title

World number two Zverev has enjoyed his best year on the Tour, reaching the semi-finals at the Australian Open and the final at Wimbledon alongside his French Open and US Open successes.

He has been aided by injuries to Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz, who swept the majors in the past two seasons, but a strengthened mentality and dedication to fitness has also helped.

"There is no-one as fit as Zverev, he is right up there," former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"You can argue about Alcaraz and Sinner, and Novak [Djokovic] and Rafa [Nadal] when they were in their prime physically, but Zverev is right up there as one of the best athletes to play the sport."

Zverev was taken to five sets in his first two matches, with both finishing in the early hours of the New York morning.

He was two points from defeat in the first round, but rallied, played his way into form and did not drop a set from the third round until the final.

Faced with a partisan crowd against Shelton, Zverev did not buckle. He kept his emotions deliberately in check and, even though he lost the third set, never loosened his grip on the match.

"I'm so admiring of his strength of character and the zen-like state he's been in since the very beginning of the match," said former British number one Annabel Croft.

"The most extraordinary thing - and I don't think I've ever witnessed it - was that he didn't realise he had won.

"It was so bizarre, but it was like he was in a trance-like state while he was playing."

His serve - one of the best on the ATP Tour - was key against Shelton.

He won 39 of 42 points behind his first serve in the first two sets and did not face a break point until the middle of the third.

Shelton broke at the end of the third set to extend the match but the American made little impact in return games from then on, winning only four of 20 receiving points in set four

Victory means he will now have the world number one ranking in his sights - he trails Sinner by 1,810 points with two Masters 1000 events and the season-ending ATP Tour finals to come.

But Zverev is a polarising figure in tennis.

In October 2023, he was given a penalty order and fined 450,000 euros (£392,000) for bodily harm against his ex-partner, with whom he shares a child.

Zverev denied the claims and lodged an objection against the order. A trial in May 2024 was discontinued after a week and there was a separate settlement between Zverev and his ex-girlfriend.

At the time, the court told BBC Sport: "The decision is not a verdict and it is not a decision about guilt or innocence."

Zverev was also accused in October 2020 of physical violence and controlling behaviour by another former girlfriend. He maintained his innocence from the start and there were no legal proceedings.

articles.title: US Open: Ben Shelton suggests rule change over champion Alexander Zverev's ball-bouncing habit
articles.summary: The 2026 US Open will go down as a triumph for Alexander Zverev. With some grumbles along the way.
articles.body:
The 2026 US Open will go down as a triumph for Alexander Zverev. With some grumbles along the way.

The German defeated Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6, 5-7, 6-2 on Sunday to capture his second career Grand Slam title, a few months after his first such trophy at Roland-Garros. It was a brilliant performance , especially on a serve Shelton only managed to break once across four sets.

That serve perturbed many opponents this tournament, but not just because of its 130-plus mph speeds and the backhand often following it. It was also the waiting.

Throughout the tournament, Zverev kept opponents on indefinite standby with his serve. There is a 25-second serve clock in between points for exactly this reason, but no such limit exists on second serves.

So Zverev was seemingly bouncing the ball upward of 10 times on every single second serve. Sometimes in excess of 20 times. It bothered his opponents, the crowd and the broadcasters, with everyone speculating what could be done about it.

That includes Shelton, who suggested a a time limit for second serves while speaking with reporters after the match :

"For a first serve you should be able to do whatever you want and use the full 25 seconds every time. I think that there should be some sort of rule — I'm not sure exactly how you would do it — limiting time on second serves. You shouldn't have unlimited time. For our sport, for the fans. I think it's tough to be sitting there for that long for the next action to happen. "I'm sure at some point it will be something that these tournaments look at just because there is such a delay in play in some matches."

"For a first serve you should be able to do whatever you want and use the full 25 seconds every time. I think that there should be some sort of rule — I'm not sure exactly how you would do it — limiting time on second serves. You shouldn't have unlimited time. For our sport, for the fans. I think it's tough to be sitting there for that long for the next action to happen.

"I'm sure at some point it will be something that these tournaments look at just because there is such a delay in play in some matches."

The ball-bouncing was addressed at one point in Sunday's match. The chair umpire gave Zverev a time violation in the fourth set after such a delay, to the loud delight of the Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd. Zverev appeared to argue he was actually waiting for a crowd clearly partial to Shelton to settle down.

Karen Khachanov, Zverev's semifinal opponent, had a similar issue with the ball bounces in their match but conceded it was within the rules:

"The way he bounces the ball, look, it annoys not only me, of course, but a lot of players, because it takes so much time. You don't know how to prepare for the serve. You are ready, and then it's another 12 bounces. "Every point like that. At the end of the day, if it's within the rules with the time between points, I cannot say anything against that, because it's within the rules. If he extends the time, he gets a time violation, so it's pretty simple as that."

"The way he bounces the ball, look, it annoys not only me, of course, but a lot of players, because it takes so much time. You don't know how to prepare for the serve. You are ready, and then it's another 12 bounces.

"Every point like that. At the end of the day, if it's within the rules with the time between points, I cannot say anything against that, because it's within the rules. If he extends the time, he gets a time violation, so it's pretty simple as that."

This stuff isn't particularly new with Zverev — you can see him bounce the ball 12 times before his first second serve in this 2026 Australian Open match — but the number of bounces definitely seemed to increase in this tournament. It is also the kind of scrutiny players start experiencing once they become multi-time Grand Slam champions.

For his part, Zverev insisted he's not trying to reach a specific number and said he actually did try to decrease the bounces while speaking with reporters after the semifinal:

"I'm not counting in my head. I'm not getting a certain number or anything like that. I don't know why it increased so much. Today it decreased again, because I saw it before the semifinals so I was like, 'OK, it's gotta go less,' but then I forget about it every once in a while and it goes up. I don't know what number it is.

"I'm not counting in my head. I'm not getting a certain number or anything like that. I don't know why it increased so much.

Today it decreased again, because I saw it before the semifinals so I was like, 'OK, it's gotta go less,' but then I forget about it every once in a while and it goes up. I don't know what number it is.

Whatever is done about the ball-bouncing, 2026 stands to go down as a career season for Zverev. He entered the year as the consensus best player to never win a Grand Slam and proceeded to go 25-2 in Grand Slams that year, losing to only Carlos Alcaraz (Australian Open semifinal) and Jannik Sinner (Wimbledon final).

Questions remain about his ability to beat modern tennis' new duopoly, but it's clear his legacy has changed this year.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev calls Trinity Rodman 'lucky charm' after beating her boyfriend Ben Shelton in US Open final
articles.summary: Tennis News: Trinity Rodman made a 200-mile trip from Washington to New York on Sunday after playing for Washington Spirit, arriving at Arthur Ashe Stadium in time.
articles.body: Trinity Rodman made a 200-mile trip from Washington to New York on Sunday after playing for Washington Spirit, arriving at Arthur Ashe Stadium in time to watch boyfriend Ben Shelton lose the US Open final to Alexander Zverev.Rodman was playing for the Washington Spirit against Boston Legacy at almost the same time as Shelton's first Grand Slam final, making it difficult for her to get to New York. But after the Spirit's 3-0 loss, the US soccer star travelled north and entered Shelton's box before the end of his 6-3 7-6(2) 5-7 6-2 defeat. She was wearing a shirt with Shelton's face on it."I knew ‌it was going to be pretty close to impossible ‌to get ‌here, but even just making the effort and trying is ⁠insane,” Shelton told reporters. "She kind of showed up as ​I was losing, which for her probably sucked."Even Zverev referred to Rodman's arrival during his on-court victory speech."Trinity, I thought you had a game today,” the German joked. "You're the lucky charm ... not today, but usually."Rodman and Shelton went public with their relationship in March 2025 and have since become one of the most visible young pairings in American sports. They regularly travel to support each other.Rodman has attended Shelton's tournaments, including his title runs in Dallas and Stuttgart this year, while Shelton has also attended Washington Spirit matches.Rodman had also watched several of Shelton's matches during his run at Flushing Meadows, including his quarter-final win over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz, which ended at 3:33 a.m., the latest finish in US Open history."We've made a lot of sacrifices for each other,” Shelton said. "We've travelled the world to try to support each other when we can."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘I just thought it was 5-1’: Alexander Zverev reveals how he missed US Open win, then calls himself the best player ‘right, right now’
articles.summary: Tennis News: Alexander Zverev had waited six years to erase the pain of his first US Open final. When the moment finally arrived, the German did not even realise h.
articles.body: Alexander Zverev had waited six years to erase the pain of his first US Open final. When the moment finally arrived, the German did not even realise he had won it.Zverev defeated American Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2 on Sunday to win his first US Open title and second Grand Slam of the year, following his maiden major triumph at Roland Garros in June. But after sealing the championship point, the world No. 2 remained behind the baseline, preparing to receive another serve.It took his team’s reaction — and a glance around the stadium — for Zverev to realise that he was now a US Open champion.‘I didn’t hear that she said, Game, set, match’Zverev said he was so locked into the contest that he completely missed the chair umpire announcing the end of the match.“In that moment, I was in the zone a lot. I didn't hear noise at all,” Zverev said during his post-match press conference. “I was in this kind of tunnel where I just didn't hear anything. Also, when the crowd is loud, it's impossible to hear the umpire, so I didn't hear that she said, ‘Game, set, match’. At the end of the day, I just forgot the score. I just thought it was 5-1 instead of 6-2.”The victory was particularly significant for Zverev, who had lost the 2020 US Open final to Dominic Thiem after leading by two sets and being two points from the title.The German believes those scars have now finally disappeared.“I think the scars of the 2020 final, they kind of disappeared after I won in Paris,” Zverev said. “I said it at Wimbledon. Even though I lost the final, I enjoyed the match. I enjoyed being in the Grand Slam final, I enjoyed playing on Centre Court, and I enjoyed playing in front of an amazing crowd, in front of some celebrities and all that. I enjoyed doing that.”“Whereas before winning in Paris, I felt a lot of stress all the time, because there was always a question mark: ‘Will I ever win one?’ What I think now is just more of a joy to play those kinds of finals.”Zverev’s verdict on SheltonShelton was playing in his first Grand Slam final, but Zverev was impressed by how much the 23-year-old had developed.“I think he's very talented, but he's very close to the hard work as well,” Zverev said. “You see him and his father all the time after matches, before matches, working on different things, and every single year he keeps improving something.”“I just played him today. I think this was the best backhand he's ever hit against me, the most consistent power. There was everything there.”Zverev recalled their first meetings and said Shelton had added a new level of consistency to his game.“I remember a couple of years ago when I first played him, he was always dangerous, he always had that serve, and he always had that forehand. But if you played three, four balls back, there would be an error, and that was absolutely not the case today.”‘Right, right now, probably yes’Zverev’s second major of the season also put him in a unique position in 2026. He is the only player to have won multiple Grand Slam titles this year, while Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz have won one each.Asked whether he now considers himself the best player in the world, Zverev was reluctant to make an absolute claim — but conceded that, at this particular moment, he may have the strongest case.“I don’t know how to answer that,” he said. “You have to take everything into consideration. With Jannik Sinner being injured, Carlos Alcaraz coming back from injury after four months, right now, this moment, probably yes."“Both of them healthy, both of them at the top of their game? Maybe not. But if we say right, right now, with Jannik being injured and Carlos coming back from injury, maybe.”Sinner missed the US Open through injury, while Alcaraz returned to Grand Slam action in New York after a four-month injury layoff.Zverev, however, was quick to acknowledge that the hierarchy could look very different when all three are fully fit.“Four or five months ago, when both of them were healthy, I wasn’t [the best player in the world],” he said. “I was losing to Jannik all the time. If everyone is healthy, I think Jannik is still ahead. It’s as simple as that,” he added.Zverev is 0-5 against Sinner this year, having won just one set against the world No. 1 — a tiebreaker in the Wimbledon final.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Shut these guys up': Fans slam commentator as 'get healthy Alcaraz and Sinner' remark spoils Zverev's US Open win
articles.summary: Tennis News: Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton in the US Open final on Sunday to win the second Grand Slam title of his career, but the German's victory was follow.
articles.body: Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton in the US Open final on Sunday to win the second Grand Slam title of his career, but the German's victory was followed by criticism of John McEnroe's closing remark on the broadcast.The top-seeded Zverev beat eighth seed Shelton 6-3, 7-6 (7/2), 5-7, 6-2, stopping the American from becoming the first US man in 23 years to win a Grand Slam title.Zverev also moved past the memory of his 2020 US Open final loss, when he was two points away from victory before Dominic Thiem came back to win in five sets. It took six years and two major final defeats for Zverev to win his first US Open title.However, instead of ending the broadcast by focusing on Zverev's victory, McEnroe turned his attention to Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, the two players who were not in the final."Get healthy, Carlos [Alcaraz] and Jannik [Sinner]," McEnroe said.The comment quickly went viral on social media, with some fans criticising McEnroe for making the remark immediately after Zverev had won his second Grand Slam title of the season.Alcaraz had been knocked out by Shelton in the quarterfinals after returning from a wrist injury, while Sinner missed the entire tournament with a knee problem.Reacting to McEnroe's remarks, one fan wrote, "Not liking a player doesnt mean you disrespect their achievements. The commentary box should feel embarrassed for saying that!! Very poor in taste and disrespectful I am sure they wouldn't like it if same disrespect was shown to the one they back or like."Another fan pointed out that Alcaraz had been part of the tournament and had lost to Shelton, writing, "But you are aware that Carlos participated? And lost against the guy who had no chance against Zverev in the final?"Another fan said, "I hope Zverev beats either of them or both to get another slam soon and shut these guys up,"Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: George W Bush to Donald Trump: None of Federer, Nadal and Djokovic in top 10 rankings for first time since 2002
articles.summary: Tennis News: Last time none of Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic were in the top 10 of the ATP rankings, George W Bush was the US president, euro had .
articles.body: Last time none of Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic were in the top 10 of the ATP rankings, George W Bush was the US president, euro had just entered circulation, and Ronaldo had just led Brazil to the FIFA World Cup title.For the first time since October 2002, the men's top 10 no longer includes any member of the Big Three. Djokovic, the last active player from the trio, dropped from No. 5 to No. 12 in the latest ATP rankings released on Monday after his early exit at the US Open.Federer retired in 2022 at the age of 41, while Nadal retired in 2024 at 38. Djokovic, now 39, is the last member of the trio still playing.The rankings underline how much tennis has changed. In October 2002, Lleyton Hewitt was the world No. 1. Nearly 24 years later, his 17-year-old son Cruz Hewitt is now beginning his own professional career.Djokovic's fall came after a first-round defeat to Mariano Navone at the US Open. It was his earliest Grand Slam exit in 20 years, dating back to the 2006 Australian Open, and the first time he had lost his opening-round match at the US Open."I've been very proud of all the achievements in the past, but now is now," Djokovic said after the defeat in New York.Djokovic remains the most successful men's singles player in Grand Slam history with 24 major titles, ahead of Nadal's 22 and Federer's 20.The numbers behind the Big ThreeFederer entered the ATP top 10 later in October 2002 and stayed there until the end of 2016. During that period, he also spent a record 237 weeks as world No. 1.Nadal broke into the top 10 in April 2005 during his rise on clay as an 18-year-old. He stayed in the top 10 for a record 912 consecutive weeks before dropping out in 2023.Djokovic entered the top 10 in 2007 and went on to spend a record 428 total weeks as world No. 1.A new generation takes overThe current rankings continue to be led by Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz.This season has been very different from last year. Sinner and Alcaraz met in three of the four Grand Slam finals in 2025, but they did not face each other in any major final in 2026.Alcaraz missed both the French Open and Wimbledon because of a right wrist injury, while Sinner withdrew from the US Open with a right knee injury.While Alcaraz won the Australian Open and Sinner won Wimbledon, the most consistent player this season has been Zverev. He won the French Open and the US Open, finished runner-up at Wimbledon and reached the semifinals of the Australian Open.Even after winning his second Grand Slam title of the year, Zverev stopped short of calling himself the world's best player.“If everyone is healthy, I think Jannik is still ahead,” Zverev said after beating Ben Shelton in the US Open final. “It's as simple as that.”Ben Shelton, after reaching his first Grand Slam final at the US Open, climbed five places to world No. 4 in the latest rankings.Rybakina replaces Sabalenka at No. 1On the women's side, Elena Rybakina moved to world No. 1 after winning her second Grand Slam title of the season at the US Open, having also won the Australian Open earlier this year.Rybakina's victory ended Aryna Sabalenka's run of 99 consecutive weeks as world No. 1.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2009, Juan Martin del Potro beat Roger Federer to win the US Open for Argentina; 17 years later, he remains the last non-European Grand Slam winner
articles.summary: Tennis News: There was a time when men's Grand Slam tennis had champions from across the globe. Australia, the United States, Argentina and South Africa all produc.
articles.body: There was a time when men's Grand Slam tennis had champions from across the globe. Australia, the United States, Argentina and South Africa all produced major winners, adding different styles and stories to the sport's biggest tournaments. But the landscape has changed dramatically.Juan Martin del Potro's historic 2009 US Open triumph remains the last time a non-European man won a Grand Slam singles title. The Argentine defeated five-time defending champion Roger Federer in a five-set final at Flushing Meadows, producing one of the biggest upsets of his career. More than 17 years later, that victory still stands as the most recent men's singles Grand Slam title won by a player from outside Europe.Since then, the men's Grand Slam scene has been dominated almost entirely by European stars. Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic drove the first part of that era, before the next generation led by Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev continued the trend.The numbers make the change particularly striking. From 2010 through 2026, every completed men's singles Grand Slam has been won by a European player. The only exception in terms of a tournament not having a champion was Wimbledon in 2020, which was cancelled because of the COVID-19 pandemic.From the Big Three to Alcaraz, Sinner and ZverevFederer, Nadal and Djokovic were responsible for much of Europe's extraordinary dominance during the 2010s. Nadal repeatedly ruled Roland-Garros, Djokovic collected titles at the Australian Open, Wimbledon and US Open, while Federer continued to add major trophies.Andy Murray of Great Britain also broke through during this period, winning Wimbledon twice and the 2012 US Open. Switzerland's Stan Wawrinka, Croatia's Marin Cilic and Austria's Dominic Thiem were among the other Europeans to lift Grand Slam trophies.The transition to the next generation has not changed the geographical pattern.Spain's Alcaraz won the 2026 Australian Open, completing a career Grand Slam at just 22 years old. He became the youngest man to win all four major singles titles.Germany's Alexander Zverev then captured his maiden Roland-Garros title in 2026 before adding the US Open trophy yesterday in New York. His Paris triumph also made him the first German man to win Roland-Garros in the Open Era.Italy's Jannik Sinner, meanwhile, continued his rise by winning Wimbledon in 2026.YearAustralian OpenFrench OpenWimbledonUS Open2010Roger FedererRafael NadalRafael NadalRafael Nadal2011Novak DjokovicRafael NadalNovak DjokovicNovak Djokovic2012Novak DjokovicRafael NadalRoger FedererAndy Murray2013Novak DjokovicRafael NadalAndy MurrayRafael Nadal2014Stan WawrinkaRafael NadalNovak DjokovicMarin Cilic2015Novak DjokovicStan WawrinkaNovak DjokovicNovak Djokovic2016Novak DjokovicNovak DjokovicAndy MurrayStan Wawrinka2017Roger FedererRafael NadalRoger FedererRafael Nadal2018Roger FedererRafael NadalNovak DjokovicNovak Djokovic2019Novak DjokovicRafael NadalNovak DjokovicRafael Nadal2020Novak DjokovicRafael NadalCancelledDominic Thiem2021Novak DjokovicNovak DjokovicNovak DjokovicDaniil Medvedev2022Rafael NadalRafael NadalNovak DjokovicCarlos Alcaraz2023Novak DjokovicNovak DjokovicCarlos AlcarazNovak Djokovic2024Jannik SinnerCarlos AlcarazCarlos AlcarazJannik Sinner2025Jannik SinnerCarlos AlcarazJannik SinnerCarlos Alcaraz2026Carlos AlcarazAlexander ZverevJannik SinnerAlexander ZverevThe sport has produced major champions from outside Europe before, with the likes of Pete Sampras, Andre Agassi, Jim Courier, Michael Chang, Arthur Ashe, Guillermo Vilas and Del Potro proving that Grand Slam success is not restricted to one continent.But the modern era tells a very different story. From Federer and Nadal to Djokovic, Alcaraz, Sinner and Zverev, European players have controlled the biggest stages for more than a decade and a half.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Zverev pone por delante a Sinner de él... y de Alcaraz: "Si todos están sanos, Jannik sigue por delante"
articles.standfirst: El alemán reconoce el nivel del número 1 del mundo, actualmente fuera por molestias en la rodilla derecha
articles.summary: El alemán reconoce el nivel del número 1 del mundo, actualmente fuera por molestias en la rodilla derecha
articles.body: Alexander Zverev tiene tiempo para ganar su segundo grande en Nueva York y honrar el nivel de sus máximos rivales en el circuito. El italiano no ha estado sobre las pistas de Flushing Meadows por molestias en la rodilla derecha. En la rueda de prensa postpartido, al alemán le preguntaron sobre si, a día de hoy, se considera el mejor jugador del mundo: "Hay que tener en cuenta todo. Con Jannik Sinner lesionado y Carlos Alcaraz regresando de una lesión después de 4 meses… en este momento probablemente sí". Pero el bicampeón de Grand Slam no dudó en darle su lugar a Sinner y Alcaraz, sobre todo al italiano: "Con ambos sanos y en su mejor nivel, tal vez no. Pero si decimos justo ahora con Jannik lesionado y Carlos regresando de una lesión, tal vez. Hace 4 o 5 meses cuando ambos estaban sanos, no lo era. Perdía contra Sinner todo el tiempo. Si todos están bien, Jannik sigue por delante. Es tan simple como eso", declaraba Alexander Zverev. El de Hamburgo ha sobrepasado a Sinner por 700 puntos en la 'race' rumbo a las ATP Finals de Turín.

articles.title: Toby Samuel: Brit to make Davis Cup debut after 'surreal' year
articles.summary: Briton Toby Samuel is to make his Davis Cup debut for Great Britain after what he calls a "surreal" 12 months.
articles.body:
Toby Samuel says it was "one of the best moments in my life" when he was selected in Great Britain's Davis Cup team to face Ecuador this weekend after a breakthrough year.

The 23-year-old was handed his maiden Davis Cup call-up after a rapid rise over the past 12 months, climbing into the top 100 in the world rankings and making his debut in three Grand Slams.

"It's surreal being in this position now from where I was eight, nine months ago, [when I was] hopefully trying to play some Challengers, and now I'm sat here ready to play the Davis Cup - it's crazy," he told BBC Points West.

Samuel joins Arthur Fery, Cameron Norrie, Henry Patten and Lloyd Glasspool in the squad to face Ecuador at London's Copper Box arena.

Samuel breaks more new ground with first win at a Slam

Fery named in GB Davis Cup team to face Ecuador

Samuel, who is from Winchester and trains in Bath, was in New York having just made his US Open debut when he was told the news.

"I was out in New York walking around when I got a call up from Leon [Smith] the captain saying, 'congratulations, you've been selected,'" Samuel added.

"It was unbelievable, it was one of the best moments of my tennis life, to get called up to that, it's what every British player wants, to represent their country and play for their country."

At the US Open, Samuel claimed his first victory in a Grand Slam with a dominant win over Tomas Machac before losing to 18th seed Jiri Lehecka in the next round.

It has been a year of firsts as Samuel also reached the main draw of the French Open, coming through three rounds of qualifying before losing to world number eight Alex de Minaur in the first round proper.

Weeks later, he was handed a wildcard entry at Wimbledon and took Czech 15th seed and French Open semi-finalist Jakub Mensik to five sets.

"At first it was a completely new experience, I was pretty nervous going to those tournaments, seeing the top guys there in the locker rooms and playing against them - I was sort of shaking a little bit on court," Samuel said.

"But after the second or third time I did it I got more used to it and I felt like I was a lot calmer on the court, which helped me to go deep."

Stepping up to the top-tier tournaments has meant mentally and physically there has been a lot for Samuel to learn this past year.

With Challenger Tour matches played over three sets, this is the first time Samuel has consistently played five-set matches.

Being able to play for three, four or even five hours is a "new thing", although he feels his serve and forehand have improved significantly.

"Before they were good but they weren't really scaring people," he said. "Now they're my biggest weapons and I can take matches with them."

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz regresa a los entrenos con la mirada puesta en la Laver Cup
articles.standfirst: El murciano encadenará su viaje a Londres con tres torneos en la gira asiática
articles.summary: El murciano encadenará su viaje a Londres con tres torneos en la gira asiática
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, según ha podido saber MARCA, regresó el domingo a los entrenamientos (en e apartado físico), cinco días después de caer en los cuartos del US Open, y esta semana ya vuelve a ejercitarse en las pistas de Murcia con la mirada puesta en lo que viene. Su siguiente cita en el calendario es la Laver Cup de Londres, del 25 al 27 de septiembre. Desde la capital británica volará a Tokio ((30 de septiembre al 6 de octubre) para defender título en el torneo de categoría 500 y después estará en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái (7 al 18 de octubre). En su regreso a Europa realizará una parada en Riad para disputar por tercera edición consecutiva el Six Kings Slam ((21 al 24 de octubre). Allí comparte cartel con Jannik Sinner, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz y Alex de Miñaur.

articles.title: Atlanta’s Ben Shelton bid to be 1st American winner of US Open since 2003 ends in loss to Zverev
articles.summary: With history on the line for the US Open, Ben Shelton falls short of bringing home the win for America. He'd aimed to be the first American to win since 2003...
articles.body:
Ben Shelton had already told the fans he was really going to need them.

"I'm gonna need you guys on Sunday to bring the energy," the American had told a cheering Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd when he beat compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the U.S. Open semifinals, setting up his first Grand Slam final. "We're going for it here."

Well, Shelton sure had Sunday's crowd. As opponent and ultimate victor Alexander Zverev himself correctly estimated, "99.9%" of the crowd seemed to be supporting Shelton.

The brashly confident and appealing 23-year-old was trying to become the first American to win a Grand Slam title since Andy Roddick won the U.S. Open in 2003 — and the first Black man to win the tournament since Arthur Ashe in 1968.

But with all that history on the line — and maybe even because of it — it wasn't enough.

Shelton fell to a far more accurate and experienced Zverev, 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2, as the hard-serving German extended what has been a stellar year in which he's captured two Grand Slams and come close to knocking Jannik Sinner off his world No. 1 perch.

It cheered Shelton, the No. 8 seed, constantly — from the moment he arrived on court, and whenever he exhibited intermittent flashes of brilliance. "Let's go Ben!" they chanted, and sometimes "USA! USA!" Especially in the third set, when Shelton prevailed. The crowd roared, and settled in for a change of direction.

But it didn't happen. Zverev quickly broke for a 2-0 lead, then broke again for 5-2, and won the match more quickly than many anticipated — apparently including Zverev, who didn't realize at first that he'd actually won.

Minutes later, at the trophy ceremony, a downcast Shelton recovered to smile and then charm the crowd, thanking everyone from, first, God, to his family and his team, and down to his driver and "the security guards who make me smile every day."

He saved his final thanks for the fans of New York, especially those "who stayed until 4 in the morning." That was a reference to his epic quarterfinal win over No. 2 seed Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set thriller that will be talked about for years — and only partly because it concluded at 3:33 a.m., the latest finish ever at the Open.

Speaking to the media later Sunday, Shelton was subdued, but clearly focused on the future.

"I'm motivated," he said. "Disappointed with how today went (but) happy with how I fought throughout the week, two weeks. Excited with the progress that I feel that I've made, but yeah, this one stings 100%.

"It's on to the next," he said. "Try to keep getting better and show up in Australia even stronger than I showed up here."

If Shelton had been troubled by the weight of history and the dreams of a long-denied tennis nation, he did not mention it.

But earlier in the week, he seemed to consciously downplay that angle.

"Like, yes, I can think about how cool this moment is and what I'm playing for," he had said after his semifinal. "But at the end of the day, I'm here in New York, I'm hanging out with my team, I'm with my homies playing a little bit of tennis, and I've been able to downplay the moment pretty well."

Asked Sunday what had made the final against Zverev so challenging, he first cited the incredible accuracy of the German's serve.

"He's got the best serve in tennis," Shelton said. "I broke him today for the first time in 66 games. I think you combine that with as good as he is as a tennis player outside the serve, how complete he is, he's gotten so much better at the net. He's an elite mover at 6-foot-7. He's got a lot of length, so he returns really well. Solid from the baseline and one of the fittest guys on tour too."

And he noted his own lack of consistency.

"I definitely didn't execute from the ground the way I wanted to," he said. "I didn't hit my forehand well today … I made too many errors, and I think that's the big piece from me. I want to be more lethal with my forehand."

Shelton also made clear he was annoyed with how many times Zverev was bouncing the ball before serves — a practice that even brought Zverev some boos from the crowd, as when he sought to complain about a time violation issued by the umpire.

Shelton said the umpire had told him to get to the line earlier to return serve. "I was, like, 'He can start his routine whenever he wants. I promise you there will never be a time where he serves and I'm not ready. But I shouldn't have to sit at the line — you know, if he's bouncing the ball 20 to 25 times, I shouldn't have to just sit there for that."

Summing up his experience in the biggest match of his life, though, Shelton made clear he was focusing on the positives.

"It's such a cool moment," he said. "Walking out on that court today, there's nothing like it. I've never felt anything like that before. It's an addicting feeling being in positions like this."

"Obviously for me it sucked the last couple of Grand Slams sitting at home for 10, 11, 12 days while the tournament was still going on, watching everyone else run through the draw. You know, it's motivating. Losing in the final is also motivating, but this is the position I want to be in."

And he made clear he knows he needs to keep improving.

"I don't think I'm anywhere near the player that I want to be," Shelton said. "I think I'm a great competitor. ... But yeah, to win on Sundays, you've got to play a very, very high level of great tennis.

articles.title: El 'Big 3' desaparece del top10 24 años después
articles.standfirst: La salida de Djokovic, único miembro activo en el circuito, cierra un ciclo de más de dos décadas
articles.summary: La salida de Djokovic, único miembro activo en el circuito, cierra un ciclo de más de dos décadas
articles.body: Corren tiempos de cambio por las calles de la vieja guardia. Por primera vez en 24 años, ningún miembro del 'Big 3': Novak Djokovic, Rafa Nadal y Roger Federer, aparece en el top10 del ranking ATP. La reciente salida del serbio, único miembro de los tres tenistas en activo, es la respuesta. Su derrota en la primera ronda del US Open ante Navone, le ha hecho caer desde el quinto hasta el decimosegundo puesto. El suizo y el español, retirados en 2022 y 2024, respectivamente, han visto esta semana al último miembro del exitoso grupo de los 66 Grand Slam salir de la cima compuesta por los 10 mejores tenistas del mundo más de dos décadas después. El 14 de octubre de 2002 es la fecha de inicio de este dominio ininterrumpido en el top10 del ranking. Fue cuando un joven de 21 años nacido en Basilea, llamado Roger Federer, ingresó por segunda vez en estas posiciones. Se mantuvo hasta el 7 de noviembre de 2026, acumulando 734 semanas consecutivas. Por su parte, Rafa Nadal hizo su primera aparición (con 18 años) en este exclusivo grupo el 25 de abril de 2005, hasta el 6 de marzo de 2023, fijando su marca en un récord de 912 semanas. El último en unirse a los 10 primeros fue, el todavía presente en el circuito, Novak Djokovic. El 19 de marzo de 2007 inicio su periplo de 553 semanas hasta el 6 de noviembre de 2017, ahí permaneció nueve meses fuera del top10. Regresó el 20 de agosto de 2018 para continuar por 421 semanas más, hasta hoy. Los tres mayores ganadores de la historia coincidieron dentro del top10 en dos periodos. El primero, durante 503 semanas (casi 10 años). Marca su inicio la fecha de entrada del serbio (19 de marzo de 2003) hasta la primera salida del suizo (17 de noviembre de 2016). El segundo periodo ocurre entre el 16 de julio de 2018 y el 18 de octubre de 2021, fecha en la que Roger Federer dejó de pertenecer a la élite. Durante 673 semanas (no consecutivas) el 'Big 3' coincidió entre los 10 mejores jugadores del mundo.
